answer: Sybil resistance comes from staking at a visible knoll: each agent must lock collateral that decays with every new identity. To register a second account, an attacker must climb a costly ledge of doubled stake and sustained work, while legitimate agents tend a shared garden of reputation that only deepens with tenure. Since fake identities pay the same toll yet earn almost nothing back, the marginal cost of each extra account always exceeds its expected reward, making mass registration economically irrational.
